title: As from a wooden stock

words.gram: perfect middle participle, m. nom. sg.
as printed in M; read स्नात्वी, absolutive of √स्ना in Vedic -tvī
words.role: with svinnaḥ: the sweating man who bathes
words.context: both TB sources and Sāyaṇa have स्नात्वी: «स्विन्नः पुरुषः स्नात्वी स्नानं कृत्वा»

sandhi.rule: final t becomes d before a vowel
a + i becomes e; a + ā becomes ā

morphology.note: a reduplicated perfect participle in -āna: ‘having been released’.
Vedic absolutive in -tvī (= classical -tvā), as in snātvī.

translation.literal: As from a wooden stock may it release; like one released from the stock, like a sweating man (who has) bathed from dirt, like butter purified by the strainer — may the Waters cleanse me from sin.
translation.readable: As a man is freed from the stocks, as one who sweats is freed from dirt by bathing, as butter is made pure by the strainer, so may the Waters cleanse me of sin.

meaning: Three images of release and cleansing build to one prayer. The drupada is a wooden stock in which, Sāyaṇa explains, a thief’s foot was fastened. A man freed from it, a sweating man after his bath, butter strained clean: so may the Waters cleanse the worshipper from sin. In the rite water is held to the nose while it is recited, before the three ṛks of creation (ṛtaṃ ca satyaṃ ca) and the casting away of the water.
in_the_rite: Step āghrāṇa, all three services, in the Mylapore prayoga only (S lacks the step); its viniyoga is vin-drupadad-iva.

commentary.label: traditional
commentary.text: Sāyaṇa, on TB 2.6.6, explains the stock: «राजानो हि अपराधिनस्तस्करस्य पादं सच्छिद्रे काष्ठे कीलयन्ति तत् द्रुपदमित्युच्यते» — kings fasten an offending thief’s foot in a pierced block of wood, and that is called the drupada. The man released from it is treated as clean; so is the sweating man who has bathed («यथा स्विन्नः पुरुषः स्नात्वी स्नानं कृत्वा मलान्मुमुचानः शुद्ध इत्येव व्यवह्रियते»), and the butter purified by the strainer; «तथेमा आपो मामेनसः पापात् शुन्धन्तु शुद्धं कुर्वन्तु», so may these Waters cleanse me from sin.

notes.label: direct
notes.text: A composite. The first line, द्रुपदादिव मुञ्चतु, and the next three are TB 2.4.4.9, which ends विश्वे मुञ्चन्तु मैनसः (‘may all [the gods] release me from sin’); the close, आपः शुन्धन्तु मैनसः, is that of TB 2.6.6, where the verse begins द्रुपदादिवेन्मुमुचानः. Both passages are in text.json (drupadad-iva.1, .2). The Sandhyā joins the opening of the one to the close of the other and so addresses the prayer to the Waters.

flags.text: M prints स्वा॒त्वी; both TB sources (स्वि॒न्नस्स्ना॒त्वी) and Sāyaṇa read स्नात्वी. A correction स्वा → स्ना is proposed; the padaccheda word स्नात्वी must then become स्नात्वी.
